title: Audit logs & admin activity review with Harbor Finance
summary: Redwood team walked Harbor Finance through what audit logs capture, export/streaming options, retention defaults and configurable policies, RBAC/SSO interactions with audit events, and encryption/KMS considerations. Customer requested sample schema, a short export PoC to their S3, and confirmation on retention/legal-hold workflows.
topics: RBAC/SSO events and who/what is logged
encryption at rest and KMS key rotation events
access to raw logs for compliance audits
next_steps: Redwood to share audit-log schema and sample export within 2 business days
Set up a short PoC export to Harbor's S3 bucket - target week of 5/25
Leah to schedule a follow-up technical deep dive for KMS key rotation and HSM integration
Send SOC2+ISO artifacts and SOC2 section that references audit logging
action_items: Samir: Share audit log schema and example JSON export (due 2026-05-18)
Priya: Provide S3 bucket details and IAM role for PoC (due 2026-05-20)
Leah: Run a sample export and validate field mappings with Harbor (due 2026-05-25)
Jordan: Attach SOC2/ISO pack link in CRM deal notes (due 2026-05-18)
transcript:
Header: 2026-05-16 14:30 PDT | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Leah (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM), Maya (CISO), Ethan (Head of Platform), Priya (Security Engineer)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda - audit logs, what we capture, export options, retention, and any questions on encryption/KMS. Maya, do you want to kick off with your main concerns?

[00:12] Maya: Yeah thanks, um, main things for Harbor are - we need assurance logs include admin activity, role changes, SSO events, API key usage, and any exfil/export attempts. Also, retention policy, and how we can export to our SIEM.

[00:30] Leah: Great, so on Redwood side we capture a broad set of events: user auth events (SSO, MFA), API key creation/deletion, role and permission changes, admin console actions (user invite, deprovision, model pinning), model deployment and rollback events, and data export operations. We also record request metadata like IP, request id, and timestamp.

[01:02] Priya: Sorry, when you say data export ops - is that user-triggered downloads and programmatic exports? Do you log the payload or just the event?

[01:10] Leah: Good Q. We log the event metadata - who initiated, timestamp, resource id, destination (e.g., S3 path or webhook endpoint), size, and a reference id. We do not store customer data payloads in the audit log itself. There are short cases where we capture small hashes for verification but not full content.

[01:45] Ethan: And retention - what's the default? We have regulatory requirements for 7 years for certain ops, but maybe we can tier?

[01:55] Jordan: Quick answer: default retention in hosted plan is 90 days, but for enterprise we support configurable retention policies and long-term export. You can push logs to your S3/Cloud storage or stream to SIEM for indefinite retention.

[02:12] Maya: Ok, and how do you guarantee integrity? If someone rotates keys or an admin deletes entries, is there an append-only store or WORM option?

[02:25] Leah: We have write-once append semantics for primary audit collections; deletion requires admin escalation and is logged as well. For higher assurance, customers can configure real-time streaming to their own S3 or SIEM. We also support signing each event with a service-level signing key so you can verify event sequences. Full WORM retention is supported via the customer's S3 bucket using S3 Object Lock for legal hold.

[03:05] Priya: How about KMS - do you support customer-managed keys? Key rotation?

[03:12] Leah: Yes, for Private and Dedicated we support CMK via AWS KMS, and we have HSM integrations for on-prem. Key rotation is supported; rotation events (who rotated, when, new key id reference) are all emitted to the audit stream. Important note - when you bring your own CMK, we encrypt the persisted logs with that key and we also include KMS operation events in the audit log.

[03:45] Maya: Great. What about RBAC - is every permission check logged? Like, when a token is used to access an endpoint, is that a line in the audit log?

[03:58] Leah: We log permission-granting actions (role create/update/delete, membership changes), and we log critical authorization failures and admin-level accesses. We don't log every single read access at token-level for every single API call by default because that would explode volume, but there is an option to enable verbose access logging for specific resources or for a sampling window.

[04:30] Ethan: For SIEM integration - do you provide JSON schema and sample payloads? Any out-of-the-box connectors?

[04:38] Samir: We have schema docs and sample exports. We also have built integrations with Datadog and Splunk (forwarders) and provide a syslog/webhook/S3 exporter. For customers using Sumologic or other SIEMs, we provide a JSON line format that your ingestion can parse.

[05:05] Priya: Is there support for streaming real-time to our Splunk HEC or a syslog endpoint?

[05:12] Leah: Yes - streaming via webhook or syslog is supported for near-real-time. For Splunk HEC we typically recommend the webhook + batching to HEC. We can also provide a small sidecar that forwards events if you want guaranteed ordering.

[05:40] Maya: Audit logs tie into our compliance reporting. For SOC2 evidence, would Redwood provide signed exports or an audit trail we can present?

[05:50] Jordan: We can produce signed export bundles and retention metadata. Our SOC2 pack documents the logging coverage and we include sample signed logs on request. We'll attach that pack.

[06:12] Ethan: A few specifics: 1) We need admin activity to include console UI actions and API actions - e.g., if someone pins a model or changes a rollout, we want to see the pre/post state. 2) We need identity to be resolvable to SSO identity (Okta) not just internal id. 3) We need the ability to export raw logs for forensic analysis within 24h.

[06:40] Leah: On 1) we capture action type, target resource, and a delta summary - pre/post where feasible; large objects we link to a snapshot id. On 2) we map internal user ids to SSO identity (Okta email and external id) in the event. On 3) exports can be initiated ad-hoc and streamed to your S3; for enterprise customers we can also set near-real-time replication to your storage so forensic access is immediate.

[07:22] Priya: About legal hold - if legal needs to preserve logs, can we apply holds without Redwood staff intervention?

[07:30] Jordan: If you stream to your own S3 you control lifecycle and holds. For logs retained in Redwood-managed storage we have a legal-hold workflow where a written request triggers retention suspension; however, deletion or tampering would still be logged and requires elevated approvals. We can also set up account-level holds for enterprise agreements.

[08:00] Maya: Any PII in logs? Need to know for GDPR.

[08:07] Leah: We avoid storing PII by default. Identity fields are SSO email and user id; for GDPR customers we can redact or pseudonymize additional fields. We have controls to mask IPs and user agents if required.

[08:30] Ethan: How granular are timestamps and timezone handling? For us UTC is preferred.

[08:36] Leah: All logs are timestamped in UTC with ISO8601. We also include local tz metadata where available.

[08:50] Priya: Can we run queries on the logs inside Redwood console for quick triage?

[08:58] Leah: Yes - there is an audit log viewer with filtering by event type, user, resource, and time window. For heavy analysis we recommend exporting to your SIEM.

[09:15] Maya: One more - detection of suspicious activity: account takeovers, anomalous exports - do you provide any alerts?

[09:24] Leah: We have basic anomaly rules and can send alerts to PagerDuty/webhook/email. For enterprise customers we can plug into your SIEM to run advanced detections.

[09:40] Samir: Quick show of sample schema - I'll paste the link in chat after - it includes fields: event_id, timestamp, user.email, user.id, event.type, resource.type, resource.id, action, details.delta, src.ip, req.id, dest.endpoint, export.size, signature, kms_key_id (if encrypted).

[10:05] Ethan: Good. About encryption-at-rest for logs - is that always on? How's key rotation handled?

[10:15] Leah: Encryption at rest is always on. For hosted customers we manage keys by default; enterprise customers can bring their own CMK. Key rotation events are logged; when you rotate a CMK we create new envelope keys and record entitlement. If you're using BYOK, you control rotation cadence.

[10:40] Priya: If we rotate keys, will historical logs be re-encrypted with the new key or stay encrypted by the old key?

[10:47] Leah: They remain encrypted under the envelope key that was used at write time. If you want re-encryption we can run a rewrap job, but by default we keep original encryption to preserve chain-of-trust.

[11:10] Maya: Regarding admin deletions - you mentioned deletions are logged. Can you show an example event for deletion?

[11:18] Leah: Example: event.type=admin.action, action=delete_user, user.id=..., user.email=..., target.user.id=..., timestamp, performed_by=..., reason=manual_by_admin, audit.signature=...; plus a deletion-record which references the retained snapshot id.

[11:48] Priya: For the PoC - will you push a week of sample logs with a mix of events so we can validate SIEM ingestion and field mappings?

[11:55] Samir: Yes, we'll include a week of synthetic and anonymized real-like events. We'll coordinate on the fields you need.

[12:10] Ethan: SLA questions - if our replica stream to S3 fails for a period, is that queued or do we drop?

[12:18] Leah: We buffer and retry for a configurable window. For enterprise we provide guaranteed delivery windows and will failover to persistent queueing. Failures and retries are emitted as audit events too.

[12:40] Maya: One more - are admin actions tied to ticket IDs or change requests? We want correlation with our ITSM.

[12:48] Leah: We allow you to attach external refs in the event payload like ticket_id or jira:1234. We can auto-include a change request field if you pass it in during the call.

[13:05] Samir: Ok I'm going to summarize and list deliverables. We'll send the schema and sample export. We'll do a PoC export to Harbor's S3 and follow up with a deeper KMS/session key rotation deep dive. Anything else?

[13:20] Maya: Please confirm the pre/post state capture for model deployments - we need to be able to see which model version was active before and after a rollout.

[13:30] Leah: Confirmed - deployment events include previous_version and new_version fields, and we log the rollout policy and who kicked it off.

[13:40] Priya: Also, please include details on masking user IPs and pseudonymization options in the docs.

[13:50] Jordan: Noted. Wrap up: Samir will drop the docs, Leah will run the PoC, Priya will provide S3 role. We'll reconvene after PoC. Thanks everyone.

[14:02] Samir: Thanks all. End call.

Note: transcript includes some ASR errors and mis-attributions, occasional filler words, and short overlaps typical of recorded meeting outputs.
